A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LangSplatV2 research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite relocation and expanded back matter.

before.justification: v1 reports original runtime measurements, localization and segmentation results on three datasets, and component and hyperparameter ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including Tables 1–11.

M1.justification: The global codebook, normalized top-K sparse coefficients, joint learning, and CUDA sparse splatting remain unchanged in Sections 3.3–3.4 and Algorithm 1. The new evaluation appendix documents procedures without establishing a method modification.

E1.justification: Both versions use LERF, 3D-OVS, and Mip-NeRF360 with the same tasks and scenes. Figure 6's revised caption mentions Mip-NeRF360, but those examples and their identification in the appendix text already appear in v1.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding benchmark and resource comparisons. LangSplat-512D in v2 Table 7 is the existing 512-dimensional LangSplat comparison from v1 Table 11. Newly discussed related methods are not added to the evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The reported datasets, metrics, training budgets, model choices, and hardware are retained. Appendix C newly documents dataset-specific post-processing and semantic-level selection for existing experiments; it does not establish a protocol revision or rerun.

E4.justification: The component timing ablation, codebook-size and sparsity studies, and qualitative examples are retained. v1 Appendix C becomes v2 Appendix D, while the existing training-cost analysis moves into the main text.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same repeated-run LangSplat Kitchen result, 17.5 ± 1.8 correct predictions, without specifying the run count. v2 adds no seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or changed uncertainty-estimation practice; its checklist supplies no additional statistical evidence.

E6.justification: All 11 tables retain their numerical results after matching renumbering and transposition, and the qualitative figure content is unchanged. For example, LangSplatV2 segmentation IoUs remain 59.9%, 94.6%, and 69.4% on LERF, 3D-OVS, and Mip-NeRF360, respectively.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the sparse-representation assumptions, rendering factorization, and complexity argument are unchanged. Appendix C's averaging formula documents evaluation processing without introducing a new theoretical result or revising the existing derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and performance claims: removing the heavyweight decoder through sparse coefficients and a global codebook, efficient sparse splatting, and the reported rendering and querying speedups.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly explains using coarse whole/part semantic levels for simpler 3D-OVS scenes and all three levels for more complex Mip-NeRF360 scenes. Existing result interpretations, training-cost limitations, and inherited CLIP-bias limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix C specifies relevance-map smoothing, semantic-level selection, normalization and thresholding, and dataset-specific use of semantic levels. These disclosures improve documentation of existing evaluations, although the threshold value and pooling settings remain unspecified. Existing training details and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens the literature discussion with a dedicated Gaussian-splatting acceleration survey covering quantization, structural simplification, and rasterization, including CompGS, Gaussian grids, C3DGS, Speedy-Splat, and SORT-Free Splatting. It also adds generative-reconstruction discussion. This extends v1's narrower compression discussion while retaining its central positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds an evaluation-details appendix, a NeurIPS checklist, acknowledgments, and expanded related-work prose, and moves the training-cost discussion into Section 4. The existing scientific narrative and method exposition are largely retained, with limited wording corrections.

P2.justification: The training-cost table is transposed and moved from appendix Table 11 to main-text Table 7. Figures and tables are repositioned, Figure 1 is resized, and Figure 6's dataset caption is corrected. The underlying visual content is retained without a substantial redesign.

improvement.justification: Appendix C improves reproducibility by documenting previously underspecified evaluation processing, and the expanded related-work discussion provides better context for the acceleration contribution. Moving the unchanged training-cost comparison into the main text also makes the efficiency tradeoff easier to assess. These are useful documentation gains, although some evaluation parameters remain unspecified and the empirical evidence and uncertainty reporting are unchanged.
